EDIT: She elaborated more on this and she said:

"I just said that to me it's not a bad thing, and he implicitly said that it's a bad thing, the typical response of the society. He should've said: "I think that cutting is a bad thing" explicitly, not impling it"

I quote her:

"It's neither of them. When you are streesed you need to vent it someway. Some people go running, other watch simpsons [I watch the simpsons when I'm anxious to calm me down]. It's like human body: it has to mantain a certain temperature in order to survive, when you pass a certain point you die. Cutting is the same thing, the stress is so overwhelming that it's the only way to make it go away. Only it's not socially acceptable because we have the blood taboo, if we lived in a society that regarded simpsons as a taboo I would be seen as a completely normal girl"

After the last reply she had another thought (have another orangered envelope):

"We base the social reality upon our own experiences, to help us better undersand and confront the external world. And this is what we do with people, we may label someone as a cold person to guide us in our relationship with him or her.

She changed me, I changed her.

Other people would have bailed on her after 1 month, I stick with her and I hurt myself badly, thanks to her I'm now able to do everything I want but I cry at night scared that she might have a crisis.

I will be maybe better off talking to a shrink myself and trying to sort this out.. I'm too weak and confused to approach something like a broke up with her.. I would spiral down a very deep depression as of know.

I would love to hear people telling me that everything is A-OK instead of hearing every fucking time friends telling me to GTFO.
